help.first.title: First steps
help.first.intro: These steps take you from the start screen to a calendar file with your own meetings. They use the Scrum template; the other templates work the same way.
help.first.step.start: Open the view {control}. As long as the workspace has no team, it shows the start screen {title}.
help.first.step.open: Choose {control}. A short wizard asks a few questions.
help.first.step.create: Choose {control}. The new team gets the roles, cadence, categories and meetings of the template, and the person attends every meeting of the Product Owner.
help.first.step.team: The field {field} already holds a name, and {start} is today. Keep them or change them, then choose {control}.
help.first.step.people: Under {heading}, type a name into the field Product Owner, for example your own. Separate several names with commas.
help.first.step.frame: Under {heading}, check the time zone, the region for holidays and the planning horizon, then choose {control}.
help.first.step.meetings: Open the view {control} and check the meetings of the template: {when}, {next} and {participants}. To change a meeting, choose {edit} in its row.
help.first.step.calendar: Open the view {control}. Each day shows its meetings; choose a day to see its details.
help.first.step.load: Open the view {control}. The table {table} lists your person's meeting hours per week, and the column {fte} shows their share of the working week.
help.first.step.exchange: Open the view {control}. Under {scope}, choose {person}, then select your person in {pick}.
help.first.step.export: Choose {control} and save the .ics file. It holds the meetings of your person in the planning horizon.
help.first.next: How to add the file to Outlook, Google Calendar or Apple Calendar is explained under {ics}.
help.first.other: To look around first, choose {example} on the start screen: it opens a workspace with two sample teams. {file} opens a workspace file you already have.
help.views.title: The views
help.views.intro: Choose a view in the list of views. Above every view are the buttons for the workspace file ({new}, {open}, {save}, {saveAs}); Calendar, Weeks and Load also have the filters {role} and {person}. At the top of the sidebar is the {team} selection; the button {actions} next to it holds {plan}, {addTeam}, {rename}, {duplicate} and {delete}. While there is no team yet, the Calendar shows the start screen instead.
help.views.filters: The filters apply to {calendar}, {weeks} and {load}, which show the selected team. {role} narrows them to what one role of the team attends. {person} shows the meetings of one person across all teams; the calendar then also marks meetings that overlap. While a person is selected, {role} cannot be changed; set {person} back to {all} to use it.
help.views.calendar: {month} shows a month, {week} a week. {prev} and {next} page back and forth ({prevWeek} and {nextWeek} in {week}). {today} returns to the current date, or to the start of the planning horizon when today is outside it. Each day shows its meetings in the colour of their category and marks public holidays, school holidays, the cadence and milestones. Days outside the planning horizon and non-working days are marked too.
help.views.calendar.legend: Below the month, the legend names the categories of the meetings shown; the hours at the top right of a day are its meeting hours.
help.views.day: Choose a day to open its details next to it: every meeting with its time, hours, category, repeat rule, roles and, with several teams, its team, plus the public holiday and overlaps. {edit} opens the meeting in the Meetings view. When {skip} is on, meetings on a public holiday are listed as skipped. {close}, the Escape key or a click outside closes the details.
help.views.weeks: One row for every week of the planning horizon: its Monday, its events (cadence, milestones, public holidays, school holidays and weeks with high load), the hours of each role and the {total} with a bar. The current week is marked {current}. {warn} and {cadence} show only those weeks.
help.views.load: {role} at the top shows the total, the hours of every role with their share of the {hpw} and the FTE, and the peak week. {chart} shows every week of the planning horizon, with the average as a line and weeks with a warning in orange. {base} shows the hours per week of every category and role. {person} lists every person across all teams with the average hours per week, the FTE and the peak week. {warnings} names, per person, the weeks in which they are clearly above their average or above the FTE limit. {calc} explains the numbers.
help.views.meetings: The meetings of the selected team. {add} opens the form for name, category, repeat rule, time, duration, preparation and the roles taking part with their share. With {scale}, the duration follows an assumption of the team. Every row has {edit}, {duplicate} and {delete}. Below the table you manage the {categories} and their colours; they apply to the whole workspace.
help.views.team: Everything that belongs to the selected team. Under {members}, a member is a person with a role; one person can have several roles. Under {cadence} you set the type ({sprint}, {flow} or {pi}), the length in weeks and the start date. {cycles} hold the milestones that meetings can refer to. {assumptions} are numbers such as the team size, which scaled meeting durations use.
help.views.settings: Everything that applies to the whole workspace. {general} holds {language}, {region}, {timezone} and {hpw}. Below are the {workdays}, the {horizon}, {skip}, the {thresholds}, and the lists of {roles} and {people}. Every person has their own {hours}. The language can also be switched below the list of views.
help.views.templates: Under {builtin} you create a team from Scrum, Kanban or SAFe. You can also import a template file or export a team as a template; see {more}.
help.views.export: {export}: under {scope}, choose a team, a role or a person. Set the period with {from} and {to}, an optional {reminder}, and under {include} whether public holidays, school holidays and milestones are added. Then choose {button}.
help.views.import: {import}: choose {button} and select an .ics file. Choose the team under {team} and the roles under {roles}, then check the list of items found. Items marked {duplicate} are not selected; items Caldence cannot use are listed under {skipped} with the reason.
help.region.title: Regions and holidays
help.region.intro: The {region} decides which public holidays and school holidays Caldence knows.
help.region.import: If your region is not in the list, choose {import} and select a region file. Caldence adds the region to the workspace and selects it; {undo} removes it again. Imported regions are saved in the workspace file.
help.region.remove: To remove an imported region, first select another region, then choose {remove}.
help.region.warn: If the {horizon} ends after the date until which the school holidays of the region are known, {settings} and {weeks} show a warning. A workspace with an unknown region uses no holidays until you choose a region or import its region file.
help.calc.title: How the load is calculated
help.calc.duration: Duration: a meeting lasts its {duration}. If {scale} is ticked, the duration is {base} + {perUnit} × the value of the chosen {assumption}, rounded up to the next multiple of the value in {grid}.
help.calc.share: Share and preparation: every role under {participants} takes its {share} of the duration; 0.5 means every other time. {prep} adds that percentage of the time on top.
help.calc.members: Members: every member of the team with that role gets these hours.
help.calc.holidays: Holidays: when {skip} is on, meetings on public holidays are skipped and count no hours. School holidays do not change the load.
help.calc.base: {baseTable} and the role tiles in {roleTable} show the typical week of the repeat rules, independent of the planning horizon and holidays. One-off meetings and meetings relative to a milestone are not part of it. The percentage and the FTE refer to the {hpw}.
help.calc.average: Average: {personTable} adds up the hours of every week of the planning horizon, across all teams, and divides them by the number of weeks.
help.calc.fte: {fte}: meeting hours per week ÷ the {hours} of the person. 1.0 is the whole working week.
help.calc.warn: {warnings}: a week is listed when a person has more than {warnFactor} × their average hours, or when its FTE is above {maxFte}. Both are under {thresholds} in {settings}.
help.calc.cost: Costs: when {hourlyRate} in {settings} is filled in, Meetings and Load show the {costs} card. A meeting costs its hours (with share and preparation) × the number of members in the role × the rate; a role without members counts as one person. Per week follows the typical week, “in the horizon” adds up all meetings of the planning horizon without holidays. Without a rate, no costs are shown.
help.calc.example: Example: a 60-minute meeting with 50 % preparation and share 1 counts 1.5 hours. For a person with 40 hours per week, 8 such meetings a week are 12 hours, or 0.30 FTE.
help.where.title: Settings or assumptions?
help.where.caption: Where each value is edited
help.where.intro: Values for the whole workspace are in {settings}. Values that belong to one team, such as its {assumptions}, are in {team}. Meetings and their categories are in {meetings}.
help.templates.title: Templates
help.templates.apply: Apply: in {templates}, choose {apply} for Scrum, Kanban or SAFe, check the field {teamName} and choose {create}. The new team gets its roles, cadence, categories and meetings and becomes the selected team; {open} takes you to it. {undo} removes it again. The start screen {start} offers the same templates.
help.templates.import: Import: choose {importButton} and select a template file. Check the {preview} and the field {teamName}, then choose {create}.
help.templates.export: Export: under {exportHeading}, choose the {team}, enter a name in {name} and choose {exportButton}. You can share the file, and others can import it.
help.templates.people: A template holds no people. Add people in {settings} and give them their roles in {teamView}.
help.files.title: Files and autosave
help.files.format: A workspace is one file named like plan.caldence.json.
help.files.buttons: {new} starts an empty workspace. {open} reads a file. {save} writes to the open file. {saveAs} writes a new file. If there are unsaved changes, {new} and {open} first ask whether to save them.
help.files.status: Next to the buttons you see the file name, or {untitled}, and whether there are {unsaved} or the file is {saved}.
help.files.fallback: Browsers without file access download the file on Save and ask for it on Open.
help.files.autosave: Caldence also saves your work in this browser, so a reload brings it back. Autosave is no replacement for saving a file. If the browser does not allow it, the bar says {autosaveOff}.
help.files.privacy: Nothing is sent anywhere. Your data stays on your device.
help.install.title: Install and offline use
help.install.install: Caldence can be installed from your browser (install icon in the address bar or Add to Home Screen). After the first visit it also works offline.
help.install.update: Caldence looks for a new version every hour and whenever you return to it. When there is one, a notice says {available} {reload} saves your work in this browser and switches to the new version; {later} hides the notice.

help.keyboard.intro: Caldence can be used with the keyboard alone. In the list of views, the arrow keys, Home and End switch between views.

help.a11y.title: Accessibility
help.a11y.text: Caldence is built to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA in German and English, in light and dark mode. Every view works with the keyboard and is built for screen readers. The accessibility statement describes how this was tested and lists known limitations.
